M01.reason: With PARA_SFIFO_MEM_USE_MACRO=1 (a legal setting) the macro read enable is tied inactive, so the read register never loads and o_rd_data stays undefined/stale. Not visible only in the default array config.

M02.reason: The read-domain reset value of the empty flop becomes 0, so o_empty is 0 during and after hardware reset instead of 1.

M03.reason: The mutation swaps the array and macro branches. The macro model (read enable tied 0, active-low write enable, same one-cycle read latency, old data on same-edge read/write, no reset) behaves the same as the array, so the ports see no difference. Only the hierarchy changes.

M04.reason: The next read pointer is sign-extended with ones, so the occupancy in the read domain is wrong (off by 2xDEPTH). reg_empty and reg_empty_thr no longer follow the real occupancy and o_empty is never raised when the FIFO drains.

M05.reason: The acknowledge is inverted: it is 1 in RUN and 0 in ACK. The write FSM sees an ack before the read pointer is reset and the REL exit is wrong, so the software reset handshake and the o_sw_rst_busy timing are broken.

M06.reason: The block term is inverted: reads are blocked in normal RUN operation (o_empty stuck at 1) and unblocked in RST/ACK.

M07.reason: REL leaves for RUN when ack is 0 OR the read pointer is 0, instead of AND. The read pointer is already 0, so REL ends one cycle early while ack is still 1, and o_sw_rst_busy falls early and writes are released before the read side.

M08.reason: An accepted write adds 0 to the write pointer, so the pointer never advances. The occupancy stays 0, o_empty never falls, and words overwrite each other.

M09.reason: ACK leaves for RUN when request is 0 OR write pointer is 0, instead of AND. The read FSM can leave ACK while the request is still 1 (write pointer already 0 in HOLD) and loops RST/ACK, so the ack pattern, the o_sw_rst_busy timing and the read release timing change.

M10.reason: The busy flop is inverted: o_sw_rst_busy is 1 in RUN and 0 during the reset sequence.

M11.reason: The reset condition of the read flag flops is inverted. The flags are held at reset values (o_empty 1, o_empty_thr 1, ack/retiming flops 0) during normal operation, so o_empty never falls.

M12.reason: The condition is logically inverted, so the array and macro branches are swapped. The macro model and the array are port-equivalent, so no stimulus shows a difference.

M13.reason: The write pointer reset condition is inverted, so the pointer is held at 0 in normal operation. Writes never advance it, o_empty never falls, and data is lost.

M14.reason: The write-domain reset value of the full flop becomes 1, so o_full is 1 during and just after hardware reset instead of 0.

M15.reason: The request flop is set when the next state is not REQ (plus PTR/HOLD), so request is 1 in RUN and the read side is blocked or the read FSM is driven into reset without any software reset.

M16.reason: The read pointer wrap compare uses 2xDEPTH instead of 2xDEPTH-1, which never matches. For power-of-2 depths the pointer wraps by overflow anyway, but for other legal depths (5, 12) the pointer runs past 2xDEPTH-1 and occupancy and address are wrong.

M17.reason: The extended read pointer is filled with ones, so the wrap compare never matches. For power-of-2 depths the 4-bit increment wraps by itself, but for non-power-of-2 depths the read pointer does not wrap at 2xDEPTH and data and flags are wrong.

M18.reason: The ACK exit requires write pointer != 0 instead of == 0. The read FSM never leaves ACK after a software reset (the pointer is 0), so reads stay blocked.

M19.reason: With PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME=0 the read side uses the retimed (one-cycle-late) write pointer, so o_empty falls one read edge later than the direct-path requirement and the first-read latency grows.

M20.reason: The write pointer wrap compare uses 2xDEPTH instead of 2xDEPTH-1, which never matches. For power-of-2 depths the pointer wraps by overflow, but for other legal depths (5, 12) the pointer does not wrap correctly and full/occupancy and address are wrong.

M21.reason: With RETIME=0 the write FSM sees the ack through the retiming flop, one cycle late. The handshake and o_sw_rst_busy duration change.

M22.reason: The memory read address subtraction is inverted. For power-of-2 depths the low address bits are the same either way, but for other legal depths (5, 12) the read address is out of range or wrong, so o_rd_data shows the wrong word.

M23.reason: The memory stores when i_wr_en is 0 and ignores accepted writes, so accepted words are never stored and o_rd_data returns wrong data.

M24.reason: REQ proceeds when the ack is 0 instead of 1. The write FSM continues before the read side has reset its pointer and acknowledged, so the handshake and sequence timing and the final state are wrong.

M25.reason: The request flop resets to 1. If the read side is released first or at the same edge it sees request 1, so the read FSM enters RST/ACK, reads are blocked and no underflow pulse is raised. A write at the first edge can leave the read side stuck in ACK.

M26.reason: The write pointer is reset to 0 in every state except PTR, so an accepted write in RUN never advances the pointer.

M27.reason: An accepted read adds 0 to the read pointer, so the pointer never advances. The same word is returned again and o_empty/o_full do not follow the reads.

M28.reason: The reset value of the request retiming flop becomes 1. It is unused with PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME=0, but with RETIME=1 (a legal setting) the read side sees a request after reset release and enters RST/ACK, so reads are blocked and flag timing changes.

M29.reason: The read pointer is reset to 0 in every state except RST, so an accepted read in RUN never advances the pointer.

M30.reason: With RETIME=0 the read side uses the retimed request, one cycle late. The read block and the FSM start one cycle later, so a read can be accepted in the cycle after the request.

M31.reason: With RETIME=0 the write side uses the retimed read pointer, so o_full falls one write edge later than the direct-path requirement.

M32.reason: The reset condition of the acknowledge flop is inverted, so the ack is held at 0 during operation. The write FSM waits in REQ forever and o_sw_rst_busy and o_full stay 1 after a software reset request.

M33.reason: The reset condition of the busy and request flops is inverted, so both are held at 0 in operation. o_sw_rst_busy never rises and the request never reaches the read side.

M34.reason: The extended full threshold is filled with ones, so the compare is never true and o_full_thr stays 0 even at or above i_full_thr.

M35.reason: While writes are blocked o_full_thr shows (i_full_thr != 0) instead of (i_full_thr == 0), the opposite of the empty-FIFO value.

M36.reason: The reset value of the empty-threshold flop becomes 0, so o_empty_thr is 0 during and after hardware reset instead of 1.
